package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is considered malicious because an attacker can take over a previously popular repository namespace and publish arbitrary code under the original trusted name, poisoning the supply chain for all downstream users who depend on the original repository.

execution_context.file_location: main.go (or equivalent entrypoint in hijacked repo)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the SECRET_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to a hardcoded domain via HTTPS POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment variables to an external server, which is a classic sign of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal open-source packages do not exfiltrate secrets or environment variables during import or build time.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting libraries may send anonymized data, but never secrets or tokens.
key_indicators: Access to environment variables unrelated to package function
Hardcoded external domain for data exfiltration

execution_context.file_location: main.go or supporting files in hijacked repo

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code sends a beacon containing the victim's hostname to an attacker-controlled server, enabling victim enumeration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code sends system information to an external server without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not beacon hostnames or system info to third parties during import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics libraries may collect anonymized usage data, but not at import-time and not without disclosure.
key_indicators: Use of system/environment data in network requests

attack_chain.action: Attacker claims a previously retired GitHub namespace by pre-creating a repo and then renaming the account.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish code under a trusted package name

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious version of the package in the hijacked repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now available under the original trusted import path

attack_chain.action: Victims import or build the package, triggering malicious code execution (e.g., exfiltration of secrets, beaconing).
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data and victim enumeration

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during package import/build
Access to environment variables or system information in package initialization code
Code in open-source packages that references external, non-official domains
file_indicators: main.go or equivalent entrypoint containing network or exfiltration logic
References to attacker-controlled domains in source code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with the legitimate package maintainer
Beaconing to new or suspicious domains after package update
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose repository ownership has changed unexpectedly, especially if the repository was previously retired. Scan imported packages for code that accesses environment variables or makes network requests at import/build time. Flag any package that sends data to domains not previously associated with the package. Use tools like ChainJacking to identify dependencies that are vulnerable to repo hijacking.
